subject: Re: DPA — Incident notification SLA exceptions & forensic export timing
messages:
From: Samantha Briggs <sbriggs@finsecure.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.example.com
Cc: Derek Hayes <derek.hayes@finsecure.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incident reporting timelines — request for DPA clause tightening

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood’s architecture this week. As we work through the DPA redlines internally, security has asked for clearer, shorter timelines on incident notification and forensic evidence handover for EU-stored customer data. Specifically FinSecure would like: 

- Initial customer notification within 36 hours of detection for incidents that materially affect our data or keys;
- Interim status updates every 24 hours until the incident is contained;
- Delivery of an encrypted forensic snapshot and manifests within 96 hours for hosted accounts in the EU;
- Subprocessor cooperation commitments (how and when Redwood will compel/coordinate subprocessors to provide evidence).

I’ve attached our suggested edits to the DPA and a short checklist of evidence types we typically request. Can Redwood accept the 36/96 timeline, or do you have operational constraints we should understand? If there are region-specific limits (e.g., cross-border export restrictions), please call them out and propose a fallback.

We’re trying to lock the DPA before our internal audit next month, so a quick confirmation would be appreciated.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Briggs
Head of InfoSec, FinSecure
(sbriggs@finsecure.com)

Attachments: finsecure-dpa-edits.docx (docx), evidence-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.example.com
To: Samantha Briggs <sbriggs@finsecure.com>
Cc: Derek Hayes <derek.hayes@finsecure.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, ben_carter@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident reporting timelines — request for DPA clause tightening

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear note and the attachment. We appreciate FinSecure’s priorities here. Quick summary from my side:

- We can commit to an initial notification email within 36 hours for incidents that meet the DPA’s threshold of probable unauthorized access to customer data.
- Forensic snapshot timing depends on (a) whether affected data is in-region, and (b) whether subprocessors hold portions of the telemetry. For EU-hosted accounts where all relevant tooling and logs are in region, we can target a 96-hour encrypted snapshot handoff.
- For cross-border situations or where a subprocessor is involved, we will need a bit more runway (we typically see 4–7 calendar days required to coordinate exports and legal approvals).
- We will include interim status updates; we propose every 24 hours until containment or until we have a concrete remediation plan to share.

I’ve attached a first-pass redline (redwood-dpa-proposed-edits.docx) that accepts the 36/96 proposal for in-region cases and adds explicit fallback language for subprocessors and cross-border legal holds. Can you confirm whether that will meet FinSecure’s audit expectations?

Thanks — I’ll loop in our legal and security leads for operational detail.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Sr. Director, Integrations & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dpa-proposed-edits.docx (docx)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.example.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident reporting timelines — legal questions on 36h/96h

Olga — reviewing Samantha’s request, high level legal guidance: 

- 36 hours for initial notification is aggressive but acceptable if scoped narrowly to incidents that meet the DPA’s "security incident" definition. We should avoid absolute language for detection time; instead: "within 36 hours of confirmation or reasonable belief of unauthorized access."
- 96 hours for a forensic snapshot in-region is OK, but we need explicit carveouts: legal holds, live investigations with third parties, and customer-requested preservation may extend timelines.
- Subprocessor cooperation: propose the clause require Redwood to use "commercially reasonable efforts" to secure timely cooperation from subprocessors, and to notify customers within 24 hours if a subprocessor refuses or requires a legal process.
- Include an exceptions table: typical durations and root causes (e.g., third-party legal process, HSM/KMS key export constraints, on-prem tenants).

I’ll provide a redline paragraph to insert into the DPA. Also flagging that the audit team often insists on an SLA escalation path: contact points, expected response SLAs from Redwood security, and an optional executive escalation for exceptions.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, olga_petrov@redwood.example.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident reporting timelines — operational constraints

Adding some operational color: 

- For hosted EU tenants with full telemetry in-region we can produce encrypted forensic snapshots and manifests in ~48–96 hours depending on the incident complexity. 96 hours should be conservative for single-node incidents; more complex, multi-cluster events may require up to 7 calendar days.
- If HSM/KMS-wrapped keys are involved, extracting decrypted payload is constrained: we can provide encrypted artifacts and logs immediately, but decrypted content may need cooperation from the KMS provider or explicit customer key rotation steps.
- Subprocessors: we have contractual SLAs with our top-tier subprocessors but many are subject to their own legal processes; obtaining exported snapshots from them is the main source of delay.
- Suggested operational language for the DPA: "Redwood will provide interim telemetry and audit logs within 48 hours of notification where technically possible; a full encrypted forensic snapshot will be provided within 96 hours for in-region hosted accounts unless a subprocessor or applicable law requires additional time (in which case Redwood will provide an estimate and escalate)."

I’ll attach the internal forensic-export-checklist (pdf) with items we typically deliver.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov@redwood.example.com
To: Samantha Briggs <sbriggs@finsecure.com>, Derek Hayes <derek.hayes@finsecure.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, ben_carter@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident reporting timelines — proposed compromise and next steps

Hi Samantha and Derek — thanks for patience while we pulled legal and security in. Proposed compromise below (text we can insert into the DPA redline):

1) Initial notification: Redwood will notify Customer by email within 36 hours of disclosure or reasonable belief of unauthorized access to Customer data affecting confidentiality, integrity, or availability.

2) Interim updates: Redwood will provide operational status updates every 24 hours following initial notification until the incident is contained or an agreed remediation plan is in place.

3) Forensic export (in-region): For hosted EU accounts where relevant telemetry and storage are maintained in-region and not reliant on a third-party subprocessor, Redwood will deliver an encrypted forensic snapshot and manifest within 96 hours of initial notification.

4) Subprocessor & cross-border exceptions: If a subprocessor is required to produce artifacts or applicable law restricts export, Redwood will: (a) use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain exports; (b) notify Customer within 24 hours that additional subprocessors or legal processes are implicated; and (c) provide a timeline estimate. In cases where legal process or cross-border approval is required, reasonably necessary additional time (commonly up to 7 calendar days) may be needed.

5) Telemetry & interim artifacts: Where immediate decrypted content cannot be provided (e.g., due to KMS/HSM), Redwood will provide encrypted artifacts, audit logs, and relevant telemetry within 48 hours where technically possible.

6) Escalation path: Redwood will include a named escalation contact list and will trigger executive escalation for exceptions to the timelines if requested by Customer.

If FinSecure is comfortable with the above language, we’ll mark the redline and route for signatures. If you need a shorter forensic-export target than 96 hours for all cases, please let us know which specific artifact types are highest priority (e.g., access logs, audit manifests, DB snapshots) so we can evaluate further.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute call to close.

Best regards,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Sr. Director, Integrations & Compliance
Redwood Inference
